entry.title: MacBook Pro OLED Display PWM Prompts Eye Strain Concerns Among Users
entry.content:
Links: macanorak.com | hacker news

Apple’s adoption of tandem OLED technology in the latest MacBook Pro models has triggered complaints from users experiencing eye strain, headaches, dizziness, and nausea. While the new display offers superior contrast, deep blacks, and touch capabilities, laboratory testing reveals a low Pulse Width Modulation frequency of 240Hz, which is significantly lower than previous Mini-LED models.

The sharp drop in modulation frequency has led some affected owners to return their devices, highlighting a tradeoff between advanced display specifications and visual comfort. Although PWM sensitivity varies widely among individuals, critics argue that manufacturers should provide better hardware controls or software mitigations, such as Apple's Display Pulse Smoothing feature available on other OLED devices, to better accommodate sensitive users.

entry.title: Mapping the Digital Gap Report Finds 63% of Remote First Nations Households Lack Free-to-Air TV Access
entry.content:
Links: theconversation.com | doi.org

A new report from the Mapping the Digital Gap project reveals that nearly two-thirds of households in remote First Nations communities lack access to free-to-air television. This decline is driven by widespread equipment failures in the Viewer Access Satellite Television (VAST) network, high replacement costs for set-top boxes, and logistical hurdles in providing technical maintenance to remote areas.

The loss of reliable television access increases reliance on prepaid mobile data and potentially less dependable information sources, compounding existing affordability challenges. Although fixed broadband adoption and streaming services are growing, community-led initiatives and targeted regional trials have demonstrated success in restoring broadcast access where standard maintenance models fall short.

entry.title: Steinar H. Gunderson Solves the Ancient Norse Fox Board Game
entry.content:
Links: blog.sesse.net | lobsters

Software engineer Steinar H. Gunderson has completely solved the ancient Norse asymmetric board game known as the Fox Game or halatafl, determining that sheep win with perfect play under standard rules. Using a compact bitboard representation, combinatorial number systems, and parallelized state propagation across 64 cores, Gunderson analyzed over two trillion possible board states over a 36-hour run.

The implementation required approximately 1,000 lines of code with no external dependencies, leveraging symmetry optimizations to manage memory and reduce the search space. Gunderson found that sheep maintain a forced win even when reduced to 19 or 18 pieces, while 11 sheep suffice against a single fox, conclusively settling a question left open by previous AI analyses.

entry.title: Antithesis Develops System Capable of Beating NetHack
entry.content:

Antithesis has developed a system capable of finding a path to victory in NetHack within five minutes on approximately 80% of game seeds. The development process integrated technical lessons learned from training agents on other titles, such as Super Mario Bros., Zelda, and Tetris. These experiences helped the team refine core mechanisms including value functions, resource management, and the pruning of doomed game states.

entry.title: European Commission Proposes Digital Fairness Act with New Restrictions on Video Games
entry.content:
Links: gamedeveloper.com | ec.europa.eu

The European Commission has released its proposal for the Digital Fairness Act, introducing strict consumer protection rules that target monetization and user experience design in video games across European Union member states. The 71-page legislative proposal includes sweeping restrictions on free-to-play features, requiring transparent real-money values for virtual currencies, prohibiting certain pay-to-win mechanisms for minors, and banning the sale of loot boxes to underage players entirely.

Additional provisions require companies to allow users to disable compulsive design elements such as push notifications and engagement streaks, while virtual currencies and in-app purchases targeting minors will be disabled by default. European industry trade bodies, including Video Games Europe and the European Games Developer Federation, have criticized the proposal, arguing that its broad definitions and age-rating criteria could heavily disrupt game development and balancing before the bill faces a formal vote in the European Parliament and Council.

Rozenek suffered a stroke that altered his voice, and the studio received his consent to use AI to bridge the gap between his current performances and thousands of lines recorded over a decade ago for the 2015 game.

Localization producer Mikołaj Szwed emphasized that the decision was an ethical exception made strictly due to Rozenek's health constraints.
